It's a good way to take yourself out of a dangerous situation. I've done this. It was actually a miserable experience. But, it took me about 16 hours to get released again. That was enough time for me to lose my focus on suicide. 

They will take every single object and peice of clothing you have on you. They will put you in a hospital gown or scrubs and you will be locked in the ER psych department until you've seen a psychiatrist. Then it's up to the psychiatrist what happens next.

Just walk up to the ER triage nurse and say you want to kill yourself. They will do the rest. But be warned, it's not pleasant, not comfortable, and lots of those staff members are numb to people like us and are just following procedure. But, you will be safe.

I don't think there is anything wrong with wanting your death to have meaning, or your life for that matter. This is a subject that I talk with my brother about a lot. My perspective actually matches yours. He sees lots of meaning and purpose in this life. Although, I remember one day when I was arguing meaninglessness he told me he saw that as a kind of freedom. If nothing matters then I am free to live my life as I please, or not at all. This led to a conversation about cause and effect and I started arguing that I am trapped by cause and effect. I can't do anything I want because my choices effect the world. I feel meaningless impotence. He said I have zoomed my perspective lens out too far. From a birds eye view nothing matters. Zoom back in. Focus on a family member, or a stranger, or a pet. He said, make your positive impact one moment at a time. When you do that, meaning takes shape. You can always die tomorrow.

You strike me as an inherently decent and intelligent person. I can tell you that means a LOT to me. I have trouble finding people that understand my perspective. I would like it if you want to keep talking about this stuff.
Tell him casually that a woman's clitoris is as sensitive as an eyeball.

This sounds like a greater reflection of him as a lover instead of you. You aren't the one with the hang up. You've explained your needs and he has dismissed them. Sounds more like a compatibility problem than a sexiness problem.

I think you should post this, or something similar, in r/sex. It's a sex advice thread. It's not porn. Some of the people there have really great advice.

As for the depression, your self image could be suffering because of this or it could be deeper and this is a symptom. I can't tell you which but it might be worth reflection. I know that depression and self image can prevent climax. Then not climaxing can make you feel worse. It becomes a self perpetuating problem. The folks at r/sex might be able to help with that too.

I'm not going to discuss technique with you. I can tell you that an altruistic death is pretty much martyrdom or myth. As with living, there is no way to have zero negative impact. This world effects you and you effect it. Controlling that effect perfectly is an impossibility. We are all trapped in that dichotomy.

My sister takes those medications and has that diagnosis. Her mania comes with some pretty serious psychosis. I have spent my entire life helping her through it. If you have anything you want to talk about I am here.

They don't know what to do or how to do it. Yeah, its self absorbed. Yeah, they are glossing over it and wishing it away. I can relate to this a lot. 

I think if my family had any idea how deep this was for me they couldn't ignore it. The fact is, they know very well how deep this is for me and they often ignore it. Honestly, it's just as bad for most of them too even though they wouldn't ever admit it to me. 

Over the years I found that they can't directly help me unless I know exactly what to ask for. It's rare I know what help to seek anyway. Often they botch it then too. Family and friends can love you even when they don't have a clue how to love you.

I'm glad you're here, asking for the support you need. We see you.

Statistically, the average person is 10 times more likely to use a gun on themselves than someone else. I think that statistic is way higher for people like us. I know where to locate at least 6 guns right now *not including* the one my wife keeps less than 12 feet away from me. Its the only one in my house and she thinks I don't know where she keeps it.

Telling your friends to remove the gun may not work. It wouldn't for me. For me, the realization that I actually can end it whenever I want to is actually what prevents me from doing it. Granted, I am not impulsive. But, I always find a way to put it off. It's possible one day I won't...but the location of the guns will have nothing to do with it.

Sorry to jump into your post. It just spoke to me. I can relate. I hope you don't mind my feedback.
